newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power prices hold steady in mild temps.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power prices hold steady in mild temps.

text.p: Spot bulk power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were mostly steady to slightly lower Monday with mild temperatures through the state and moderate power demand, industry sources said.
Forecasts called for temperatures to average two to four degrees above normal in western Texas and four to eight degrees above normal in eastern Texas into Tuesday.

Longer-term forecasts called for normal temperatures through much of the state from February 6 to 10 with the exception of the north, where below normal temperatures were expected during the same period.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Tuesday was talked at $20.00-22.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $21.00-23.00 on Friday for Monday delivery.
Non-firm on peak power for Monday delivery was notionally pegged lower at $18.00-20.00 from $20.00-22.00 on Friday.

Firm off-peak Tuesday ERCOT deliveries were pegged at lower at $11.00-13.00 from $15.00-17.00 on Friday, while non firm off peak power was pegged at $9.00-11.00 from $13.00-15.00 on Friday, the sources said.
March ERCOT peak power was assessed at $20.00-20.50 from $20.50-21.00 on Friday, while July/August peak power was said to have traded at $24.80, although the trade was not confirmed.
